correctness.rationale: For each target maximal segment, finitely many images of all other orientations meet it in only finitely many points; strong invariance forces an image of a preceding-orientation source segment to cover a nondegenerate subinterval. Every source segment yields at most one target, so N_(i+1) ≤ N_i. The cyclic inequalities force equality and a bijection, which in turn forces exact target coverage by excluding finitely many intersections. Segment permutation cycle length is divisible by n, omega sets are strongly invariant, and the separate direct F(H) calculation rules out H with no dynamical hypotheses. No experimental extrapolation or unverified nonstandard lemma is used.

value.rationale: García Guirao 2026 Section 11 explicitly asks whether the H-shaped connected continuum can occur as a Cournot omega-limit; the unconditional obstruction solves this concrete motivated realizability question. The orientation-count and permutation theorem are geometric finite-skeleton invariants useful for rejecting entire families of candidate omega shapes, and extend to n-dimensional cyclic maps. The contribution is a structural impossibility beyond the source conditional classification, not a routine parameter substitution or arbitrary slice.
